source: Gascheau 1843 and Routh 1875 as restated in Schwarz, Bazso, Funk and Zechner 2016 (arXiv 1608.00784, read 2026-10-30); Murray and Dermott 1999 ch. 3 (not opened); report reports/lagrange-trojans-2026-10-30.md

mu_crit.basis: (1 - sqrt(23/27)) / 2, the largest m2/(m1+m2) for which L4 and L5 are linearly stable in the circular restricted problem (Schwarz et al. 2016, text of section 1)

finite_trojan_rule.basis: the secondary plus the trojan under about 4 percent of the host, as TROY III (arXiv 2407.04677) uses it per docs/design/research/oddity-rates.md WR10; the paper's own text for the rule was not read

tadpole_limit_deg.basis: Murray and Dermott 1999: the libration amplitude past which a small-mass tadpole becomes a horseshoe (recalled, not opened)

leading_share_range.basis: no source read: Jupiter's L4 swarm outnumbers its L5 by about 1.6 to 1 (recalled), so the leading share runs from equal to about 0.62; a draw inside it

ecc_max.basis: no source read for a limit: Cresswell and Nelson 2009 (arXiv 0811.4611) keep e under 0.02 in discs and the Jupiter Trojans reach about 0.3 (recalled); a lane measures it with an N-body run

inclination_max_deg.basis: no source read for a limit: Earth Trojans are stable below 15 degrees and between 24 and 37 degrees (arXiv 1812.01244); the Jupiter Trojans reach about 40 (recalled)
